title: vscode web / Saving and sharing work
content:
## Saving and sharing work

When working on a local file in the web, your work is saved automatically if you have [Auto Save](/docs/editing/codebasics.md#save--auto-save) enabled. You can also save manually as you do when working in desktop {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} (for example **File** > **Save**).

When working on a remote repository, your work is saved in the browser's local storage until you commit it. If you open a repo or pull request using GitHub Repositories, you can push your changes in the Source Control view to persist any new work.

You can also continue working in other environments via [Continue Working On](#continue-working-in-a-different-environment).

The first time that you use **Continue Working On** with uncommitted changes, you will have the option to bring your edits to your selected development environment using **Cloud Changes**, which uses a {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} service to store your pending changes. This is described further in the [GitHub Repositories](/docs/sourcecontrol/github.md#continue-working-on) doc.
